findings.title: 25ms page budget starts before the transaction, so a busy host yields ticks that do zero work and never advance the cursor
findings.detail: observeVerdictPage (line 454) and observeCloseoutPage (line 149) compute `started = performance.now()` / `deadline = started + 25` BEFORE `db.transaction(...).immediate()`. All lock acquisition, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and first-statement preparation are charged against the budget, and the page loops only check `performance.now() >= deadline` at the TOP of the first candidate iteration — there is no guaranteed-minimum-one-candidate rule. If >25ms of wall clock elapses before the first row, the call returns 0 outcomes, advances no cursor, and writes no pending row. I proved this deterministically: injecting a 30ms synchronous stall into the transaction's first prepare made `observeVerdicts` return 0 with 5 eligible verdicts present, while the immediately following unstalled call returned 5. The same shape exists in clarifications.ts:85 (`deadline` before the transaction; `inspected` can be 0 so the learning_cursor never moves) and terminal-row-archive.ts:555 (`callDeadline` before the transaction; the `pageStarted + 25 > callDeadline` guard can break `archiveLoop` before any page is read). This fails exactly under the wedged/contended-Bridge condition the change exists to survive, so observation, clarification sweeping, and DB hygiene can all stall indefinitely while looking healthy. It is also the live cause of nondeterministic test failure: an ordinary parallel run of the changed suites on this machine produced 2 reds (outcomes.test.ts:353 and verdict-cursor.test.ts:138, both `observeVerdicts(NOW)` returning 0 instead of 1); a re-run of the identical command passed 116/116.

findings.title: Hard wall-clock assertions (<50ms / <100ms) on a 434MB fixture are wired into the required unit-tests matrix and flake at a high rate
findings.detail: ci.yml:200 adds `observation performance` as a blocking row in the `unit-tests` matrix, and because ci-test-costs.json records filesMs=37703 (>=2500) the same file is ALSO in `serialFiles`, so it additionally runs inside a regular teamlead shard — two independent chances to red per CI run. The assertions at lines 219/221 are raw wall-clock maxima over 5 samples. I ran this test once on this machine and it FAILED on the first attempt: `auto_merge_narrow_gate` sample 3 = 111.92ms vs `toBeLessThan(100)`, while the other four samples were 4.6/7.1/14.3/7.1ms — a single ~15x outlier is enough to red the gate. The PR's own ledger agrees: engineering/doc/FLY-2563-bridge-loop-fd/performance-runs.jsonl records 12 runs of which 6 FAILED (run 1, resume-6, resume-8, resume-9, resume-11, resume-12), with run 1's tail samples at [8.4, 154.5, 8.9, 48.2, 100.1] against a <50ms bar, and implementation.md states the run-1 spike was never located. On shared GitHub-hosted runners (noisier CPU and slower I/O than this host) this will nondeterministically block the merge gate for every PR in the repo, not just this branch. Also note StateStore.fly2341-terminal-archive.test.ts:34 adds another wall-clock assertion (`toBeLessThan(200)`) on a 100k-row fixture in the same suites.

findings.title: openExistingWriter uses timeout:0, removing the 5s lock budget from the founder approval / voice write paths
findings.detail: CommDB.openExistingWriter opens with `{ fileMustExist: true, timeout: 0 }` (busy_timeout=0). It now backs the founder-reply lease (founder-reply-deliverer.ts:316), the voice gate factory (voice-comm-scope.ts:9), and question admission (question-admission.ts:60), replacing `new CommDB(path, false)` which set busy_timeout=5000. comm.db is written concurrently by the Bridge, the mailbox queue and Lead CLI processes, so a held write lock is a normal condition. Empirically confirmed against a real CommDB with a concurrent `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` holder: openExistingWriter + insertInstruction failed with 'database is locked' after 2ms, while the pre-change lease connection retried for 11.6s before failing. The failure is retry-safe at the pass level (cursor pins, next poll retries), so this is not silent loss — but each BUSY consumes one of FOUNDER_REPLY_RETRY_MAX=10 cumulative attempts in the founder-reply retry ledger (gate-poller.ts:333), and past the dead-letter age threshold a single BUSY dead-letters a founder approval message. Consider giving the scoped writer a small non-zero busy_timeout (e.g. 250-1000ms) — it still bounds event-loop blocking without discarding the lock budget entirely.

findings.title: Closeouts with payload >64KiB now produce no learning outcome at all, permanently parked with next_attempt_at=NULL
findings.detail: `if (source.closed_ms === null || source.payload_bytes > 65536) { defer(id, ..., 'invalid_source', null); return; }` parks oversize closeout sources forever (next_attempt_at NULL is never selected by the due query at line 351). The pre-change code at outcomes.ts still recorded the outcome for these rows, just with an empty payload object (`Buffer.byteLength(row.payload) <= 65536 ? JSON.parse(row.payload) : {}`) — that fallback is still present at outcomes.ts:146 but is now unreachable for oversize rows. The same cutoff applies to B2 at line 535 (`payload_bytes > 65536` on author_evidence_json), where recordVerdict likewise still has a live `kind:'oversize'` digest fallback at outcomes.ts:457 that can no longer be reached. Net effect: oversize sources silently drop out of the learning ledger instead of being recorded with degraded evidence. If the intent is to avoid parsing large payloads (which the byte-length pre-check already achieves), prefer routing them through the existing degraded-evidence path rather than quarantining them.

findings.title: Rows with payload >64KiB are never archived and therefore never deleted, so the largest rows escape retention forever
findings.detail: In the per-candidate loop, `row` is only materialized when `size <= 65536`; otherwise it stays undefined, the candidate is counted as `skipped`, and the cursor advances past it. Because each new cycle restarts the scan with a fresh cutoff (line 596), the same oversize rows are re-skipped every cycle and are never written to workflow_terminal_archive — and the append-only delete triggers (line 393) require an archive row before a hot row can be deleted. The new test at StateStore.fly2341-terminal-archive.test.ts ('retains oversize payloads...') encodes this: after the sweep, only the `oversize` row remains in session_events. FLY-2341's purpose is bounding StateStore growth, and the >64KiB rows are precisely the ones that dominate size. Consider archiving oversize rows on their own low-frequency path (or raising the per-row cap while keeping the 1MiB per-page byte budget) instead of excluding them permanently.

findings.title: A failed observation-storage migration permanently disables the observer with no health field and no alert
findings.detail: If installObservationStorage throws at boot (StateStore.ts:28065), observationStorage becomes {status:'unavailable', reason:'schema_drift'|'migration_failed'} and getShipJudgmentOutcomes() throws on every 3s tick thereafter. The only signals are a single boot console.warn and a repeated console.warn from the runtime's onError sink (plugin.ts:11214 — `onError: (code) => console.warn(...)`). getShipJudgmentObservationStorage() exists but is referenced nowhere outside observation-cursor.test.ts: it is not in the /health payload (plugin.ts:2405 adds only `fd` and `event_loop`) and has no alert kind, unlike the new bridge_fd_pressure path which got a full kind contract + routed sink + recovery probe. plan.md promised 'cursor异常诊断与生产health/告警接线' and implementation.md still lists it as pending. Without it, ship-judgment observation can be dead in production indefinitely while /health reports OK.

findings.title: Archive throughput dropped from up to 128 eligible rows per call to at most 128 inspected candidates per call
findings.detail: The old implementation let SQLite apply the full eligibility predicate inside the paged SELECT, so up to MAX_TERMINAL_ARCHIVE_PAGES_PER_CALL(2) x TERMINAL_ARCHIVE_SELECT_PAGE_SIZE(64) = 128 *archivable* rows could be retired per call. The new candidate query filters only on kind + time window, then re-checks eligibility one row at a time, so the same 128 slots are now consumed by candidates regardless of eligibility. On a table where most rows in the window are ineligible (active sessions, undelivered lead_events, unconsumed closeouts), effective retirement rate falls by the ineligible fraction, and the cycle restarts from scratch with a new cutoff once completed. This is a deliberate trade per implementation.md ('逐候选预算'), but it is worth confirming against real StateStore row distributions that hygiene still outpaces ingestion — otherwise FLY-2341's growth bound regresses. The changed test at line 891 ('does not start candidate validation after the page time budget expires', archived 2 -> 0) shows the same throughput direction.

findings.title: founderReplyDeliverPass opens a full migrating CommDB writer per pass per project purely as a presence probe and closes it unused
findings.detail: `writerDb = new CommDB(dbPath, false)` is now constructed and then closed in the same `finally` (line 2384) without a single use — the deliverer opens its own short scopes. The CommDB constructor replays installMailboxTerminalArchiveSchema + SCHEMA + the whole applyMigrations suite + purgeExpired synchronously; this is the exact hotspot the deleted FLY-1601 comment in question-admission.ts described. It now runs once per founder-reply pass per project on the Bridge event loop. If the intent is only 'CommDB exists and is migrated', CommDB.openReadonly (which already asserts the mailbox generation) or a plain existsSync would be far cheaper; if the migrating open is deliberately load-bearing, a comment saying so would prevent it being removed as dead code later.

findings.title: enqueueRestoredObservation returns status:'enqueued' even when ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING left a permanently parked pending row
findings.detail: The insert uses `ON CONFLICT(project_name,source_kind,source_id) DO NOTHING`, then unconditionally returns `{status:'enqueued', sourceId}`. If a pending row already exists with next_attempt_at=NULL (reason 'invalid_source', or 'dependency' after 10 attempts), the restore replay is a no-op: the due query at line 351 never selects NULL next_attempt_at, so the source is never re-observed, yet StateStore.restoreTerminalRow (line 8173) hands the operator a receipt saying it was enqueued. The archive's own closeout protection makes this hard to reach via the archive->restore path, but restoreTerminalRow is an operator-callable entry point. Either use DO UPDATE to re-arm next_attempt_at='' for restore_replay, or return a distinct receipt status when the conflict path was taken (`changes === 0`).
